title: Mohd Hameed v. State of Uttar Pradesh
coram: Arindam Sinha and Satya Veer Singh, JJ.
disposition: Writ disposed of; petitioner relegated to Clause 6.5
headnote: Where supply has already been restored after a 50 per cent deposit, remaining allegations of incorrect bills and repeated disconnections are to be raised as a comprehensive dispute under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. The writ is disposed of without examining the bills.
facts: Mohd Hameed sought a writ directing reconnection. On 6 August 2026 the Court recorded that the supply company had demanded a 50 per cent deposit for restoration; payment was said to have been made, but the connection was not restored. On 10 August 2026, counsel for respondent nos. 2 to 5 (the supply company) submitted that the connection had been restored. Petitioner then alleged incorrect billing and repeated disconnections over a long period, claiming 75 per cent of the demand had already been paid. The licensee's counsel disputed that account.

holding_units.holding: After restoration of supply, a consumer who alleges incorrect billing and several disconnections followed by restoration is to raise a comprehensive dispute under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. The Court does not examine the bills. The writ is disposed of.

not_decided.point: Merits of the alleged incorrect bills, 75 per cent payment, and history of disconnections
not_decided.note: Left to a comprehensive Clause 6.5 dispute. Restoration of supply was recorded as already done; the Court did not decide the bills.
